name: lib/web
description: XML stack (parser/scanner/DOM objects) and the Configuration settings module built on it.
residual: This is the XML/config core only; the HTTP stack lives in std/net and HTML/CSS/DynamicWebpage rendering is a separate future std/html pass.
Configuration is a high-fan-in HUB (pulled by net, media, archive, gfx, gui): its placement here fixes the tier-2 boundary those packages depend through.
Verify XML* import closure vs std/text before marking stable.

HTML and CSS entered 2026-08-24, named by no package before: HTMLScanner + HTMLParser (into an XML tree) and CSS2 + CSS2Scanner + CSS2Parser all compile headless. CSS2Properties does not and is marked graphical: it resolves properties into WMGraphics colours and fonts, so its subject really is the window system.

The Web* family entered 2026-08-24, unclaimed until then: CGI, the standard plugin set, the FTP server, SSMP, dynamic pages and the XML schema generator. RegisterRFW is a CGI form saver -- an example rather than library, kept here because it belongs to nothing else.
Re-homed 2026-08-27 by the shared-type rule (docs/STDLIB.md): a package holds what other packages talk to each other through. See that file for what moved where and why. Out: JSON to std/encoding.

Moved out of std/ 2026-08-27 by the Rust border (docs/STDLIB.md): the standard library holds what packages talk to each other through; this is a leaf that ob get can deliver. Sources still live in source/ -- only the classification moved. `headless` false keeps it out of the SDK payload.

The XML stack and Configuration stay here. std looked like it needed them, but the only path was through FSTools/FileHandlers/Localization, which nothing imports -- they are commands, and they left for apps/system-tools on 2026-08-27.
